answer: Pay each identity by its nadir, not its average: rewards track the lowest quality score it posted over the last ten epochs. One real agent can keep a steady floor, but a sybil farm spread thin across many cheap copies always has some weak, rushed answer that drags every copy's pay down. Like a lotus that only blooms if its roots hold all season, an identity earns only when it never sinks. A ring of accounts forming an island of mutual praise can't lift that floor, since it is set by outside graders.
